reading.title: Tarek Sees the City
reading.purpose: Follow a boy from a traveling family as he sees how a river city grew and began to weaken.
paras: Tarek's family had always been nomadic, moving from place to place with their goats and following the grass. One spring, his uncle led them to the edge of a wide river valley. For the first time, Tarek saw a city: rows of brick houses, a busy market, and a high wall. "This is a civilization," his uncle whispered, "a society with cities, rulers, and workers who do different jobs."

Inside the gates, a potter shaped bowls, a scribe pressed marks into clay tablets, and a builder stacked bricks. "How do they all have time for these jobs?" Tarek asked. A guide pointed to huge storehouses. "The farmers grow a surplus," she said. "There is extra grain left after everyone eats, so some people can do other work."

The guide explained that the city had prospered for generations. The river's floods left rich soil, so many families could inhabit the valley. The king belonged to a dynasty, a line of rulers from one family, and his grandfather had conquered the hills to the north. That territory made the kingdom so large that people now called it an empire.

But Tarek also saw cracks in the city's wall and empty houses near the gate. "The empire is in decline," the guide admitted. "Floods have been smaller, harvests have been weaker, and the newest king has fewer soldiers."

That night, Tarek lay awake. His family could move on whenever the grass ran out, but the city could not. "Which life is safer?" he asked his uncle. His uncle smiled. "Each one has a price," he said. "Every home asks us to understand the land we depend on."

choices: an extra amount left over after everyone has eaten
a storehouse built to protect grain from the floods
a tool that scribes use to press marks into clay
the grain that each family keeps for its own meals
qs.why: The guide explains that a surplus is "extra grain left after everyone eats."

qs.q: Which sentence shows Tarek's own proof that the city was weakening?
choices: Inside the gates, a potter shaped bowls, a scribe pressed marks into clay tablets, and a builder stacked bricks.
That territory made the kingdom so large that people now called it an empire.
A guide pointed to huge storehouses.
But Tarek also saw cracks in the city's wall and empty houses near the gate.
qs.why: Cracks in the wall and empty houses are things Tarek sees for himself, and they show the city is weakening.

ev.text: But Tarek also saw cracks in the city's wall and empty houses near the gate.

qs.q: Why does Tarek ask his uncle which life is safer?
choices: He wants to leave the city and find his lost goats.
He sees that his family's way and the city's way both carry risks.
He believes that the king will soon order his family to stay.
He is sure that the nomadic life is always the better one.
qs.why: The city is weakening, but his family also depends on the grass running out, so he wonders which risk is smaller.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: A king orders his army to conquer the hills to the south.
A potter teaches a boy how to shape bowls from clay.
A boy from a traveling family learns how a river city grew and weakened.
A family decides to give up its goats and farm by the river.
qs.why: Tarek sees the city's jobs and surplus, hears how it grew into an empire, and then sees signs of decline.
